title: Indian indentured labour migration
summary: After the Emancipation Act of 1834 Britain turned to contract labour from India to replace enslaved workers on its plantation colonies. The first group of 36 left Calcutta and reached Port Louis, Mauritius, on 2 November 1834. About 2 million Indians emigrated to the colonies between 1834 and 1917, under contracts whose rigidity often led to coercion.

uncertainty.note: Reading paper says the system began after the 1834 Emancipation Act with the first stream to Mauritius, but also says workers were introduced to Mauritius in 1838; Curious Indian (citing Mauritius National Archives) dates the first arrival to 2 November 1834. End 1917 is when indenture was abolished in British Guiana (Leicester paper) and the Reading paper's range.

where.historical_name: Calcutta, British India; Port Louis, Mauritius, a British colony

waypoints.label: Calcutta: terms explained at the Police Head Office on 10 September; the workers boarded the Atlas five days later.
Port Louis, Mauritius: the Atlas arrived 2 November; the workers landed 4 November.

importance.justification: Moved about 2 million Indians to plantation colonies after slavery was abolished.

audience_note: This record covers a labour system set up to replace slavery; the Reading paper says contract rigidity often resulted in coercion, and an 1838 critic called it a new slave trade. Period sources use the word "coolie".

beats.caption: In Calcutta, 36 workers agree to five years on a Mauritius sugar estate, and board the Atlas five days later.
The Atlas reaches Port Louis; Britain had chosen Mauritius as its first site for using free labour to replace slaves.
About 2 million Indians emigrate to the colonies, including the first 406 who reach British Guiana in 1838.

reviewer_note: Least sure: the 36-person Atlas details rest on Curious Indian (class other, citing Mauritius National Archives and UNESCO), the UNESCO and Aapravasi Ghat pages being unreachable or silent; sources conflict on Mauritius 1834 vs 1838. The path covers only the first voyage; Guiana 1838 is not drawn.
